newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan interbank rate closes lower, seen stable.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan interbank rate closes lower, seen stable.

text.p: Taiwan's overnight interbank rate closed lower on Tuesday as the central bank did not move to mop up excess liquidity in the banking system, dealers said.

The overnight interbank rate ended at 5.839 percent against Monday's 5.921 close -- somewhat outside the central bank's target zone of 5.00-5.5 percent -- with 30-day commercial paper staying unchanged.
Dealers said liquidity was loose as funds that flowed out of the banking system continued returning.
The expected maturation of T$13 billion in negotiable certificates of deposit later in the week further eased the liquidity situation, they added.
Banks were likely to adopt a cautious policy as the central bank appeared to prefer less-volatile interest rate movements.
The bond market was stuck in a narrow-range consolidation.
The benchmark 10-year 86/4 bond yield was traded at between 6.0225 and 6.0310.
